from_quote: I do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will faithfully execute the office of president of the United States, and will, to the best of my ability, preserve, protect, and defend the constitution of the United States.
rationale: Cites "Section i, of article II" (OCR "i" for "1") and reproduces the President's oath from this clause verbatim.
to_quote: I do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will faithfully execute the Office of President of the United States, and will to the best of my Ability, preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the United States.

from_quote: That the president of the United States shall, from tim.e to time, give Congress information of the state of the union, and recommend to their consideration such measures as he shall judge necessary and expedient
rationale: Cites "Section 3, of article II" and reproduces this clause in close, slightly abridged wording ("tim.e" is OCR damage).
to_quote: He shall from time to time give to the Congress Information of the State of the Union, and recommend to their Consideration such Measures as he shall judge necessary and expedient

from_quote: The president, vice-president, and all civil officers of the United States, shall be removed from office on impeachment for, and conviction of treason, bribery, or other high crimes and misdemeanors.
rationale: Cites "Section 4, of article II" and reproduces this clause verbatim.
to_quote: The President, Vice President and all civil Officers of the United States, shall be removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors.

from_quote: That the judicial power of the United States shall be vested in one supreme court, and in such inferiour courts as Congress may from time to time appoint.
rationale: Cites "Section i, of article III" (OCR "i" for "1") and reproduces the first sentence of this clause, with "appoint" where the clause has "ordain and establish."
to_quote: The judicial Power of the United States, shall be vested in one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish.

from_quote: a rattle brained anti-federalist, in the last Mass. Gazette, under the signature of Agrippa,
rationale: Answers the piece "in the last Mass. Gazette, under the signature of Agrippa"; the Gazette before this one (Friday, December 21, 1787) was that of Tuesday, December 18, which carried Agrippa 7.

from_quote: has asserted, that the inequality of the administration of justice throughout the states, was a favourite argument in support of the new constitution — an assertion founded on as impudent and barefaced a falsehood as ever was uttered, for the very reverse is the case.
rationale: States Agrippa's assertion that inequality was a favourite argument for the new constitution and sets out to refute it; the paragraph of Agrippa 7 that makes the assertion is worked out from its subject, since Cassius paraphrases rather than quotes it.
to_quote: the most plausible argument in favour of the new plan is drawn from the inequality of its operation in different states

from_quote: the trial of all crimes, except in cases of impeachment, shall be by jury; and such trial shall be held in the state where the crime shall have been committed; but when not committed within any state, the trial shall be at such place or places, as Congress may by law have directed.
rationale: Cites "Section 2, of Article III" and reproduces this clause nearly verbatim.
to_quote: The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury; and such Trial shall be held in the State where the said Crimes shall have been committed; but when not committed within any State, the Trial shall be at such Place or Places as the Congress may by Law have directed.

from_quote: Congress shall have power to declare the punishment of treason, but no attainder of treason shall work corruption of blood, or forfeiture, except during the life of the person attainted.
rationale: Cites "Section 3, of article III" and reproduces this clause verbatim ("daring" is OCR damage for "during").
to_quote: The Congress shall have Power to declare the Punishment of Treason, but no Attainder of Treason shall work Corruption of Blood, or Forfeiture except during the Life of the Person attainted.

from_quote: full faith and credit shall be given in each state, to the publick acts, records and judicial proceedings of every other state.
rationale: Cites "Section l, of article IV" (OCR "l" for "1") and reproduces the first sentence of this clause verbatim.
to_quote: Full Faith and Credit shall be given in each State to the public Acts, Records, and judicial Proceedings of every other State.

from_quote: the citizens of each state shall be intitled to all the privileges and immunities of citizens in the several states.
rationale: Cites "Section 2, of article IV" and reproduces this clause nearly verbatim.
to_quote: The Citizens of each State shall be entitled to all Privileges and Immunities of Citizens in the several States.

from_quote: That new states may be admitted into the Union ; but no new state shall be formed or erected within the jurisdiction of any other state, nor any states be formed by the sanction of two or more states, or parts of states, without the consent of the legislatures of the states concerned, as well as of Congress.
rationale: Cites "section 3" of article IV and reproduces this clause closely; the passage reads "sanction" where the clause has "Junction."
to_quote: New States may be admitted by the Congress into this Union; but no new State shall be formed or erected within the Jurisdiction of any other State; nor any State be formed by the Junction of two or more States, or Parts of States, without the Consent of the Legislatures of the States concerned as well as of the Congress.
